title: Enquirer’s Guide: What is a retrieval?
summary: A retrieval is anything brought back from the Stratum, including material collected on a probe.
author: The Enquirer’s Guide Desk
paragraphs: This entry from The Enquirer’s Guide answers a question often put to the Society: “What is a retrieval?”
A retrieval is anything brought back from the Stratum, including material collected on a probe.
Such objects are kept under observation because their properties can be hard to establish and may change with handling. Their labels and custody histories matter as much as their appearance.

Readers should treat the answer as an introduction rather than a final authority. Eidetic science in Alderwick is reported through measurements, disputed interpretations and careful revisions, and a respectable enquiry may properly end with further questions.
